text.content:
Beyond the Battlefield

The road matters. So do the people at its end. A warm welcome, a sound bridge and a name remembered at the right moment can carry your company farther than another weapon. Your abilities include ways to navigate these scenes, but you always begin with what your hero says and does.

Explore with purpose

Tell the DA what you examine, how you approach, and what you hope to learn. If lifting the rug reveals the trapdoor, you find it by lifting the rug. No perception roll is needed to discover a fact your action plainly reveals.

When searching involves uncertainty and a meaningful consequence, the DA calls for Reason. When someone might perceive your concealed hero, roll Agility to remain Hidden; the observer does not make an opposed roll. You need a plausible place to hide. Dice do not make you disappear in open view.

Active searching or attempting to hide in combat costs a Main Action unless an ability says otherwise. Hidden is universal, not separately tracked for each observer. Attacking or openly revealing yourself ends it. The DA judges whether movement maintains actual concealment. Invisible is different: you cannot be seen, but your location is not necessarily unknown.

Before an unscripted roll, establish what progress means and what the consequences are. A Weak search might narrow the location without exposing the answer; a Weak concealment attempt might reach cover while leaving evidence of where you went. These examples are possibilities, not automatic effects that override the scene.

Consequences that matter

A consequence is what is at stake: injury, lost time, exposure, spent supplies, a worse position or a closing opportunity. A complication adds a problem while preserving any progress already earned. A benefit gives a useful advantage. The DA explains the stakes before asking for the roll.

If you can repeat an attempt indefinitely without cost, danger or changed circumstances, the table may be better served by describing the time and completing it. If failure would seal an escape route or alert a guard, say so before rolling. Weak always means its stated progress, not an unannounced success or an automatic failure.

Work as a group

Group checks occur outside combat. The DA sets a progress target and states whether the task is binary or cumulative. Each participating character rolls an appropriate attribute, contributing 1 progress on Weak, 2 on Standard, or 3 on Strong. Add the contributions and compare the total to the target.

For a binary task, meet the target in that attempt or the task is not completed. For a cumulative task, retain progress between attempts as the task allows. The DA states the time and consequence of each attempt. You can provide Aid or contribute your own group roll, not both to the same attempt.

> Example — the swollen gate. Three heroes heave against a gate before a patrol > arrives. The DA sets a binary target of 7. Weak, Strong and Strong contribute > 1 + 3 + 3 = 7: the gate opens. Weak, Standard and Strong would total 6; the gate > would stay shut and the declared consequence would follow. Pushing a boulder > uphill might instead retain those 6 progress for a later attempt.

Crafting, deriving recipes and wound treatment do not use group checks. Their individual procedures and daily limits remain in force.

Travel and the outdoors

Ordinary travel does not require routine rolls, and HOL has no exhaustion track. The DA calls for a roll when weather, pursuit, a dangerous route or another specific circumstance creates a consequence. Supplies and time still matter. Decide what your company carries, shares, buys or obtains with its abilities.

Foraging expertise comes from an appropriate environment card. It is not a universal permission to identify every edible mushroom. Other heroes can still inspect the land, collect something they already recognize, or help in a way the scene permits. Specialist cards provide their own outcomes and limitations.

Climbing and swimming normally cost 2 movement per square, like difficult terrain. This does not make a sheer unsupported wall climbable or an impassable current safe. A specialist ability can improve the activity. Roll only when the execution is uncertain and the consequence matters.

Jumping and falling

A running broad jump reaches max(1, 2 + Agility) squares. It needs two squares of approach; without that approach, halve the maximum, rounding down to a minimum of 1. A high jump reaches max(0, 1 + floor(Agility ÷ 2)) squares and needs no approach. Spend movement for the distance traveled and land in a legal, supported, free square.

Zero high-jump squares does not mean you cannot hop over a low obstacle. The grid measures large clearances. Safe jumps within your limits need no roll; a risky landing can call for Agility. Jumping does not grant extra movement or passage through a barrier.

Falling deals 3 physical damage per complete 2 squares fallen. Round the distance down to complete pairs before multiplying; normal physical resistance applies. A fall of 5 squares deals 6 damage before resistance. A fall under 2 squares has no automatic falling damage. Exceptional surfaces and landing circumstances are DA rulings.

Talk, bargain and persuade

Speak for your character, summarize what they say, or use a mixture of both. Explain what you want and why the other person might agree. The DA portrays their interests, knowledge and limits. A roll resolves uncertainty; it does not erase their motives.

Use the attribute printed on a social ability. Without one, the DA calls for an attribute appropriate to the approach. Guile might carry a deceptive bargain; Knowledge might establish a technical argument; Reason might find the important contradiction. A useful fact or appropriate gesture can make a roll unnecessary.

A scar's intimidation Boon or persuasion Bane applies when the scar actually influences the interaction. The DA decides that circumstance, just as they decide whether a wound affects a physical activity. Personality and allegiance remain choices, not penalties assigned by a condition table.

Magic in your hands

Magic is learned through abilities and disciplines. There are no spell slots or mana pools. A spell uses the same action, attribute and outcome structure as another ability, with its printed requirements and costs. An attack spell still produces its Weak result on a Weak roll; it does not simply fizzle.

You choose a card before rolling. A line, rectangle or placed area must use its printed dimensions and range. Connected placed squares share edges. Decide targets and any damage-type choice before rolling. An illustration or evocative description does not silently make the area larger or add a condition.

Defensive interference and disruption are supplied by abilities. There is no universal spell-cancellation roll. Casting beside an enemy can provoke an opportunity attack; resolve it before continuing the spell if still capable.

Beast forms keep your own HP, attributes and wounds. They are not replaceable HP pools. Use the form's printed actions and equipment restrictions. A form does not import an entire monster entry or grant spellcasting if its rules forbid it.

Moser's law of conservation of Life energy

Healing magic transfers life energy; it does not create it freely. A Novice healing spell costs its caster 1 HP, an Adept spell 3 HP, and a Master spell 7 HP. Pay the full cost before rolling. This cost bypasses all resistance and must leave the caster above 0 HP. You cannot begin a healing spell by sacrificing your last HP. The cost applies regardless of the tradition used to describe the spell.

Healing requires a free hand. Restore the outcome's printed fixed HP, reduce it by the recipient's Life resistance, and restore at least 1 if HP is missing. Never exceed maximum HP. Healing does not erase wounds or reverse Last Words. Potions have their own fixed value and inventory procedure, without a spell outcome roll or caster cost.

> Example — energy has a price. A Novice healer at 5 HP pays 1 and falls to 4, > then rolls the spell. If its outcome restores 4 HP to a companion with Life > resistance 2, the companion regains 2. The caster cannot use the same spell at > 1 HP, because paying first would leave them at 0.

A healing spell can attack a creature whose profile says healing harms it. Use the spell's attack attribute, range and cost. Its HP result becomes Life damage; beneficial recovery riders do not help that target. This follows the ordinary player-roll procedure, with no extra opposed save.

Make, identify and derive

A crafting card grants the capability to work; a recipe describes the specific thing you can make. Recipes specify permission, tools, materials, time and output. Choose the recipes granted when learning your crafting ability. Ordinary Recipe Study offers additional eligible recipes through DP. Other recipes can be found or derived; they are not automatically on sale for coins.

Acquire the actual ingredients. Foraged materials need not be carried indefinitely; carried bundles use their printed Bulk and inventory die. Complete the recipe's full time, roll the crafting card's attribute, and increase one existing product supply by 1/2/3 inventory steps as the recipe allows. Starting from out, the first step is d4. Never exceed the recipe's cap. Check carried material supply after use.

Derivation is reverse engineering, not the same as identification. Identification cards reveal what their outcomes say; an item may require that understanding before use. A magical sword may work at once, while a tome may remain unusable until understood. A derivation card specifies its target and work interval. Exceptional objects can require years of accumulated work. No group crafting or group derivation shortens it.

Rest and development

The DA determines whether a place is safe enough to spend saved DP. Level awards are milestones, not payment for each defeated creature. Keep a record of purchases, prerequisites, recipes and scars so your development remains clear.

A wound may require repeated daily treatment even after you are ready to adventure. An inn, a friendly workshop, a healer's garden or a camp among allies can become part of the story. Rest restores what its rule says it restores. It does not refund Grit, remove a permanent scar, or refill a bottle whose inventory die is out.
